rationale: Start with a broad screening gradient at mid temperature to span the full retention range and reveal how many compounds elute, where they cluster, and whether the sample is generally too retained or too weakly retained. This gives a balanced first map for choosing the next gradient direction.

Resolution is already perfect, so the only room to improve CRF is reducing analysis time while keeping all 10 peaks and acceptable spacing. A steeper full-range gradient should compress the run and test how much time can be saved before the 6–7 cluster becomes limiting.

The 10 min gradient is too steep and collapses the central cluster, while 20 min gives excess separation and unnecessary time. A 14 min full-range gradient should recover resolution for the 5–7 region while likely staying faster than injection 1 and improving CRF.

The optimum appears to lie between 14 and 20 min, with the 6–7 pair as the limiting separation. Increasing to 16 min should give a modest resolution boost in that cluster while likely keeping the run short enough to approach the maximum CRF.

Since 14 min is near-optimal in time but the 6–7 pair is still slightly under-resolved, change selectivity rather than gradient length. Lowering temperature may alter the central cluster spacing enough to raise the resolution term above the current best without incurring a time penalty.

Lower temperature worsened selectivity, so test the opposite direction at the near-optimal 14 min gradient. A modest increase to 45 C may spread the critical mid-cluster differently and improve the limiting pair without adding a time penalty.

Temperature changes hurt selectivity, so keep 40 C and adjust the starting strength to reshape the early-to-mid part of the gradient where the critical cluster sits. Raising phi0 slightly should reduce the effective gradient span and may redistribute the 5–7 region enough to improve the resolution term while staying fast.

Increasing phi0 from 0.05 to 0.10 improved both time and the limiting resolution, so continue in the same direction while holding the other factors fixed. A further step to phi0 0.15 may give another small selectivity gain in the central cluster and push CRF closer to 1.0.

The best region is now around phi0 0.10–0.15 with 14–16 min, and the limiting pair remains 6–7. Combining the better selectivity seen at phi0 0.10 with the extra resolution margin from a 16 min gradient could lift the resolution term to 1.000 while hopefully keeping the time penalty very small.

We are very close to the maximum, so now test whether the faster phi0 0.15 condition can retain full resolution when given the extra 16 min gradient time. If it reaches a 1.000 resolution term, its shorter retention than injection 9 could remove the small time penalty and hit the maximum CRF.

Since the maximum score has been reached, only nearby methods are worth probing to look for a robustness plateau around the optimum. Raising phi0 one step while keeping the successful 16 min gradient tests whether the perfect score persists with a slightly stronger start and potentially even shorter retention.

The optimum is clearly local, so probe another nearby shape change instead of moving farther in phi0. Lowering phi1 one step slightly flattens the gradient and can improve the critical 6–7 separation while likely keeping all peaks within the no-penalty time window.

A slightly longer gradient from the known optimum shape tests whether full resolution can be maintained with only a minimal time cost increase, helping define the plateau around the maximum. This is a close neighbor to the best method and should remain high-scoring while checking robustness on the slow side.

The optimum is already found, so explore a nearby flatter gradient to map robustness on phi1 more aggressively. Dropping phi1 another step could preserve full resolution while revealing whether the perfect score region extends toward lower final organic.

With the optimum method already identified, the remaining value is robustness mapping around it. A small temperature decrease at the best gradient tests whether the perfect separation is stable to common operating variation or strongly temperature-sensitive.

Temperature sensitivity appears strong in one direction, so test the opposite side of the optimum to complete the local robustness map. This checks whether the perfect method is specifically centered at 40 C or whether higher temperature also preserves full resolution.

The optimum is very localized, but a combined nearby change can still map the high-scoring ridge. Using the strong-performing phi0 0.10 with the also strong phi1 0.90 at 16 min tests whether an alternative perfect or near-perfect method exists adjacent to the current best.

With the best method already at the score ceiling, the only useful information left is the edge of failure on the fast side near the optimum composition. Shortening the optimal shape to 12 min maps how sharply the critical 6–7 pair collapses and brackets the robustness window in tG.

The best method is already known, so one remaining useful dimension is the full lower bound of temperature to complete the method sensitivity picture. This tests whether selectivity changes continue monotonically away from 40 C or if a different low-temperature regime appears.

The low-temperature extreme severely altered selectivity, so measuring the upper extreme completes the temperature-response map around the already identified optimum. This is the last major untested boundary and may reveal whether the selectivity collapse is asymmetric with temperature.

A perfect method is already in hand, so use the remaining runs to map nearby alternatives with extra resolution margin. This condition extends the strong phi0 0.10/16 min result on the slower side and checks whether it also reaches a full resolution term with only a modest time penalty.

One informative boundary near the optimum remains on the stronger-start side. Increasing phi0 another step maps how quickly the critical 6–7 separation degrades beyond 0.20 while staying in the same otherwise optimal neighborhood.

The lower-phi1 side has only been sampled to 0.85, and the trend suggests resolution margin rises while time slowly worsens. One more step to phi1 0.80 cleanly defines that boundary of the optimum basin around the already proven best method.

Only two runs remain, and one useful untested neighbor of the optimum is the slower-side boundary at 20 min with the best composition. This completes the local tG map around the perfect method and confirms how rapidly time penalty grows once full resolution is already secured.

For the final run, map the last major untested fast-side neighbor in the high-performing region. This complements the 0.15/12 and 0.10/14–18 results and shows whether lowering phi0 can preserve more of the critical 6–7 separation at a shorter gradient.
